location.basis: Centre of our z18 mosaic. We placed it from the published position (about 22.52 N, 72.25 E) and the imagery, which shows the fenced mound with the water-filled brick basin (centre 22.5226 N, 72.2492 E) and the excavated town west of it.

main_system_reason: The brick basin is the longest straight Harappan structure at Lothal and its two long walls (each about 215 m) give the most precise direction on the site. The town walls west of it are faint and short, but they agree with the basin within their errors, so the basin stands for the layout of the whole excavated settlement.
notes: The Esri imagery is a Vantor Vivid mosaic of 27 February 2026 with real detail to zoom 18 (0.55 m per pixel). The brick basin is filled with water; we measured its walls on the pale brick rim just above the water line, which follows the top of the conserved walls. The north wall lies in shadow and we did not use it. The excavated town west of the basin is conserved as low wall stubs that are mostly faint at this resolution, and the clearest straight lines there are the pale visitor paths between the conserved blocks, which we excluded. We kept two faint town walls longer than 20 m as low-confidence lines; shorter wall stubs of 12-13 m that we inspected were dropped. The basin walls were restored by the Archaeological Survey of India on their Harappan footings, so their line reflects the Harappan structure, though restoration may have straightened the visible rim slightly.
